task_instance: Build a custom Rust fuzzer with LibAFL (as a library, following the skill's 'Custom Fuzzer as Rust Library' pattern: cargo init, add libafl/libafl_bolts deps, compose an observer, feedback, objective, state, mutator, scheduler and in-process executor into a fuzz_loop) that targets a small hand-written vulnerable function (aborts on the exact input "BUG!"), run it to completion, and verify it discovers and saves the crashing input.
evidence: Created a cargo project at my_fuzzer/ (Cargo.toml declares libafl="0.16", libafl_bolts="0.16"). src/lib.rs implements a full LibAFL fuzzer composing: ConstMapObserver (coverage), MaxMapFeedback (feedback), CrashFeedback (objective), StdState with InMemoryCorpus + OnDiskCorpus, QueueScheduler, StdFuzzer, InProcessExecutor running a harness that calls vulnerable_target() (panics on exact bytes "BUG!"), RandPrintablesGenerator for initial corpus, and HavocScheduledMutator + StdMutationalStage in fuzzer.fuzz_loop(). src/bin/fuzz.rs is a thin binary calling my_fuzzer::fuzz(). Built with `cargo build --release` (CC=clang CXX=clang++) producing target/release/fuzz with no errors. Ran `./target/release/fuzz`: monitor output showed corpus growth (0->4) and coverage signal growth (1/16 -> 4/16) as havoc mutations discovered each successive byte of the 'BUG!' prefix, then the harness panicked with 'crash: vulnerable_target triggered on "BUG!"' after 483367 executions in ~1s (383.4k exec/sec), and LibAFL's OnDiskCorpus wrote the crash to crashes/4e40e92bae1ad9a1. `od -c` on that file confirms its content begins with the bytes B U G ! (0x42 0x55 0x47 0x21), i.e. the fuzzer genuinely found the injected bug via coverage-guided mutation rather than by chance on the first try. This exercises the skill's core deliverable (composing LibAFL's modular components -- observers/feedback/objective/state/mutators/scheduler/executor -- into a working custom fuzzer, per the 'Writing a Custom Fuzzer' / 'Custom Fuzzer as Rust Library' section of SKILL.md) end-to-end inside this runtime, with no need for credentials, external services, or anything outside the sandbox. One notable finding: the exact code pattern given in SKILL.md (HitcountsMapObserver track_indices + libafl 0.13 pinned version + StdMapObserver + manual corpus insertion) hit a library-internal panic (Option::unwrap() on None in libafl-0.13.2's MapFeedback::is_interesting_default, an observer/handle lookup bug) and had to be reworked using libafl 0.16 and the project's own baby_fuzzer reference pattern (ConstMapObserver + generate_initial_inputs) to get a working fuzzer; this is a documentation/version-skew issue in the skill, not a runtime limitation.
